messages:
emma: FYI customer on Dedicated reporting weird behavior on SSE reconnects — intermittent 401s during auth rotation, then on quick reconnects they get duplicate partial generations and two billing line-items. They sent a short repro and timeline.

raj: Ugh. Do we have the session id / stream id from the customer?

emma: yes: stream_id=cli-8732, session_ts around 4498999000. They said client reconnects within ~200ms after a 401 and stream resumes but repeats last chunk.

marta: Could be race between auth rotation and resume token validation. If token rotates server-side before resume handshake completes we might accept recon and re-run chunk.

oliver: Can you paste the client's reconnect sequence? often the client does: close -> reconnect (no idempotency header) -> request resume with last_seq. If we fail to dedupe on last_seq we might regenerate last token.

emma: Customer's snippet: ```js
// pseudo client
await openStream({resumeToken: cookie});
onclose -> setTimeout(120, reconnect);
reopen without idempotencyKey -> receive repeated chunk
```

raj: Thanks. Two quick asks: (1) logs for stream_id cli-8732 (server side trace), (2) billing entries for that invoice id so we can decide refund.

deploy-bot: Deployed: sse-resume-dedupe-hotfix -> canary on dedicated-pool-7.

emma: I already collected logs and attached them to the ticket. Server trace shows: 
 - 4498999005: auth refresh triggered for customer key
 - 4498999010: session resume request accepted for cli-8732 (resume_seq=42)
 - 4498999010.2: generation request spawned for seq=42
 - 4498999010.8: second resume accepted (duplicate handshake) -> spawned generation again

marta: That pattern indicates we accepted two resume handshakes before marking the session resumed. We need to make the resume handshake idempotent on server: only the first accepted resume should spawn the generation for that seq.

oliver: Agreed. Short-term mitigation: ask customer to configure exponential backoff (min 500ms) and supply an idempotency key per user-stream. Long-term: server must atomically claim resume_seq tokens.

emma: Customer asked about refunds — billing attached two small charges for the extra token generation. billing-bot: Created billing ticket #B-2119 referencing invoice INV-9987 and flagged for manual review.

raj: For CS reply, let's include a curl repro they can test with idempotency header: 
```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Idempotency-Key: mystream-xxxx" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?resume_token=cli-8732
```

marta: We should also update SDK docs to strongly encourage `Idempotency-Key` and to delay immediate reconnects during auth rotation. Add a note: avoid reconnect < 300ms after 401 unless you intend duplicate fallback.

emma: Reply draft to customer: short, apologies + mitigation steps and workaround (use Idempotency-Key, bump reconnect delay, upgrade to SDK v1.4.2 which includes resume-claim fix). Offer provisional refund while we investigate.

oliver: From infra side, I'll add a server-side guard: when resume request arrives, attempt to atomically CAS a 'claimed_seq' for (session,seq). If CAS fails, drop spawn. That should eliminate dupe generations. I'll put a canary change behind a feature flag.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for resume-claim-guard on dedicated-pool-7. Monitoring logs for duplicate generation events.

billing-bot: Billing ticket B-2119 updated: provisional refund + hold on auto-collection until review.

emma: Customer responded: "thanks, will try Idempotency-Key and bump reconnect to 500ms; please keep me posted on refund." I'll send the customer the curl snippet and the SDK upgrade link.

raj: Nice. Follow-ups: (1) product to update SDK docs (marta), (2) infra timeline for full rollout (oliver), (3) billing final decision (billing team).

marta: I'll own docs update. ETA EOD tomorrow.

oliver: I'll promote the guard to global after 6h canary if no dupes seen.

emma: tagging internal ticket #CS-7328 and closing this Slack thread; will post resolution when done. :thumbsup:
